At first, I thought the triggers were Netflix and YouTube. Then, it started happening during games. Then, it started happening during browsing. The trend seems to be that the more CPU usage, the quicker it hits. I usually get about an hour before it hits, but that shrinks to 10 minutes if I use YouTube or Netflix.

Most of what I find online relates to Windows 8 upgrading, but I did find a handy list of things to check: 

HDD becomes unreadable -- I passed the SeaTools test.
SSD Firmware not up to date -- I don't have an SSD.
Old or damaged drivers -- I updated all the drivers.
BIOS that has not been updated -- There was an update to the BIOS. I updated the BIOS. No dice.
Hardware incompatibility -- This machine is over a year old. I haven't modified the hardware.
Hardware was not installed properly -- Same.
Overclock not done properly (in this case, do a BIOS Reset) -- I'm not even attempting this.
Malware infection -- I ran Malwarebytes, SuperAntiSpyware, Kaspersky, and TDSSKiller. I seem to be clean.

Edit to add -- I also turned off "Fast Start". Any ideas?

Update: I scrubbed and reinstalled. It seems to work now, which agrees with my belief that it was not a hardware issue.

The Go Back to Previous build might fix it, if an update screwed up your system. Last resort would be the Reset this PC reinstall, in case it is just a corrupted file.

None of these worked for me when my install got corrupted, but its worth a shot.
